design_rationale: Explicit parallel-arm RCT: "Seventy patients presenting with renal calculi <1.5 cm were equally randomized to a microperc or a RIRS group... Simple randomization was performed centrally using computer-generated random numbers."

domain_judgments.rationale: Centralized computer-generated simple randomization with allocation concealed from the operating surgeon until immediately before the procedure, and baseline demographic/stone characteristics were well balanced (all P > 0.10).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Simple randomization was performed centrally using computer-generated random numbers. Randomization was revealed to the operating surgeon just before starting each procedure."

domain_judgments.rationale: Open-label design (patients, surgeons and outcome assessors unblinded) means subjective co-interventions such as analgesic administration and intra-operative JJ stenting decisions could have been influenced by knowledge of the assigned procedure; however all 70 randomized patients were analysed in their assigned groups (effectively intention-to-treat, with the two miniperc conversions retained), and blinding is not feasible for these surgical techniques.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Neither patients nor the study authors were blinded to the procedure." ... "There were 35 patients in each group. All the patients were included in the final analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 70 randomized participants, including the 3-month stone-clearance primary outcome, with no reported losses to follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "There were 35 patients in each group. All the patients were included in the final analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome ascertainment was identical across arms but assessors were explicitly unblinded, and the primary outcome relied on ultrasonography/X-ray KUB rather than the more accurate non-contrast CT (authors acknowledge this), while several secondary outcomes (pain VAS, surgeon discomfort score) are subjective and judged by unblinded participants/surgeons.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients and authors assessing the outcomes were not blinded to the procedure." ... "The use of non-contrast CT rather than X-ray KUB for follow-up would have allowed a more accurate assessment of stone clearance, but we do not do use follow-up CT routinely"

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration number or protocol is cited, so pre-specification cannot be verified; although the primary outcome and a defined list of secondary outcomes are stated a priori with an a priori power calculation, and all appear reported in Table 3, the absence of a registered protocol leaves scope for selective reporting of the many outcome measurements and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary objective was to compare stone clearance rates and secondary objectives were to compare operating time, requirement for intra-operative JJ stenting, complications... Assuming a stone clearance rate with RIRS of 80% and an expected rate of nearly 100% with microperc, the sample size for each group was calculated as 35"

overall_summary: The trial has a robust randomization procedure (centralized computer-generated sequence, concealed until just before surgery, balanced baseline characteristics) and complete outcome data for all 70 participants, but the fully open-label design means subjective outcomes (pain VAS, surgeon discomfort, stenting/analgesia decisions) and the unblinded 3-month clearance assessment by KUB rather than CT could be influenced by knowledge of allocation. Combined with the absence of a cited prospective registration or protocol, the overall judgment is "some concerns" rather than low risk, driven by domains 2, 4 and 5.

design_rationale: The paper reports an international multicenter, prospective, non-blinded randomized controlled trial with 1:1 parallel allocation generated by computer-generated random numbers and stratified by site (NCT02519634).

domain_judgments.rationale: Sequence was computer-generated and stratified, allocation was released centrally by the coordinating center only at the time of surgical scheduling (adequate concealment), and baseline demographic, stone and anatomical characteristics were comparable between arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Parallel randomization was conducted at a ratio of 1:1, stratified by site and was carried out using computer-generated random numbers. The coordinating center revealed randomization to the operating surgeon at the time of surgical scheduling."

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and surgeons were unblinded (unavoidable for surgery, but relevant to the subjective pain outcome) and several cross-overs/postponements occurred; the primary analysis was nonetheless intention-to-treat with a supportive per-protocol analysis, so concerns are limited rather than high.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The surgeons and patients were no blinded to group assignment... In the RIRS group, three patients required conversion to SMP... Three patients in the SMP group were found to have purulent fluid in the collecting system during SMP puncture. Thus a nephrostomy tube was placed and SMP postponed"

domain_judgments.rationale: All 160 randomized patients (80 per arm) appear in the intention-to-treat denominators for both 1-day and 3-month stone-free rates, indicating essentially complete primary outcome data, although the flow diagram detail and any secondary-outcome attrition is not fully tabulated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of the 186 eligible patients, 160 patients were randomized into the two groups... Intention-to-treat analysis 75 (93.8) 66 (82.5)"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary stone-free outcome was objectively defined on imaging and assessed by blinded investigators, but the day-1 assessment relied on KUB/ultrasound (less sensitive and operator-dependent) and secondary outcomes such as VAS pain were self-reported by unblinded patients who knew whether they had a percutaneous tract.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Investigators who had not been involved and blinded to the surgical procedures performed the postoperative clinical assessment."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a pre-specified primary endpoint, sample size calculation and ITT analysis plan, but the abstract/text inconsistently describes the primary endpoint (1-day and 3-month SFR both emphasised) and no protocol was available for verification of the full pre-specified analysis set.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary endpoint was the SFR at 3-months after surgery... The trial was registered at http://clinicaltrials.gov/ (NCT02519634)."

overall_summary: Randomization and outcome completeness were well handled (central computer-generated, site-stratified allocation; complete ITT data), but the trial was explicitly non-blinded for patients and surgeons, involved several cross-overs, used a less sensitive day-1 imaging assessment and patient-reported pain outcomes, and the primary endpoint definition is inconsistently reported relative to registration. These issues yield an overall judgment of some concerns, with the effectiveness findings (SFR) less vulnerable than the subjective pain outcomes.

design_rationale: The authors state explicit random allocation to the two surgical arms: "Randomization for UMPNL or RIRS procedures was done with tossing a coin method", and describe the work as a "prospective randomized study".

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and surgeons were necessarily unblinded and each arm was delivered by a different surgeon (confounding operator with intervention), and there is no statement of an intention-to-treat analysis or of any crossovers/conversions, although no deviations are reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "one surgeon performed UMPNL, and another performed RIRS. Both are highly experienced surgeons."

domain_judgments.rationale: Coin tossing at the point of assignment provides no allocation concealment, group sizes were markedly unequal (30 vs 43), and there was a statistically significant baseline imbalance in stone location — a strong prognostic factor for the stone-free outcome that the authors themselves list as a limitation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization for UMPNL or RIRS procedures was done with tossing a coin method, and one surgeon performed UMPNL, and another performed RIRS." ... "The groups were different for localizations of the stones (p=0.020)"

domain_judgments.rationale: All 73 randomized patients appear to contribute to the reported analyses, but no participant flow, loss to follow-up or completeness of the 1-month CT assessment is explicitly reported, so freedom from missing data cannot be confirmed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of 73 patients with stone sizes of 10-25 mm, and had RIRS or UMPNL procedures were included in the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary stone-free outcome was assessed objectively by low-dose CT with a stated threshold, but key secondary outcomes (VAS pain, return to daily life, hospital stay) are subjective/clinician-influenced and were collected by unblinded patients and staff who knew the allocated procedure.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Postoperative pain was determined by visual analog scale (VAS), asked by the same physician to all patients 2 hours after surgery."

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration, protocol or pre-specified primary outcome is reported, and the headline conclusion rests on an apparently post hoc, very small subgroup analysis (lower-pole stones, n=15 vs 7) among many reported outcomes and subgroups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Therefore, we analyzed our stone-free rates in UMPNL and RIRS procedures in relation with the localizations of the stones."

overall_summary: Overall high risk of bias, driven by an unconcealed coin-toss randomization that produced unequal group sizes and a significant baseline imbalance in stone location (a key prognostic factor), together with the absence of any protocol/registration and reliance on a small, apparently post hoc lower-pole subgroup for the main conclusion. Unblinded delivery by two different surgeons and subjective secondary outcomes add further concerns.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes parallel 1:1 allocation generated with computer software (STATA v13.0 random numbers) in a prospective controlled trial: "220 patients were randomized into FURL group and MPCNL group."

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated random sequence is described and baseline characteristics appear balanced, but no allocation concealment mechanism is reported (and "stratified by site" is inconsistent with a single-center study), leaving uncertainty.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Simple random sampling was adopted, and parallel randomization was conducted at a ratio of 1:1, stratified by site, and was carried out using computer software STATA version 13.0 ... to generate random numbers."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was explicitly unblinded (unavoidable for surgery) and four MPCNL patients were excluded from analyses rather than analysed by intention-to-treat (denominators change from 110 to 106), with no ITT statement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A prospective, simple random sampling and unblinded controlled study"; "Four patients assigned in the MPCNL group had purulent fluid in the initial puncture, and the following MPCNL procedure was aborted."

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 4/220 (<2%) participants lack outcome data, with the reason reported (aborted procedure due to purulent fluid), which is unlikely to bias effect estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "FURL (n = 110) MPCNL (n = 106)"

domain_judgments.rationale: Key subjective outcomes (VAS pain, BCS comfort) were self-reported by unblinded patients who knew they had undergone a less invasive procedure, and complication/imaging outcomes were also assessed without any blinding of assessors, so knowledge of the intervention could readily influence measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The severity of pain was assessed at 6, 24, and 48 hours postoperation with a visual analog scale (VAS; range: 1–10) and Bruggrmann Comfort Scale (BCS) score"; "unblinded controlled study"

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-specified protocol/primary outcome is mentioned, many outcomes and time points are reported (BCS/VAS at times not matching the Methods, which list only 6, 24, 48 hours), and the mention of retrospective record review raises concern about selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The whole study was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee of Peking University Shougang Hospital"; "The relevant medical records were retrospectively reviewed."

overall_summary: Although allocation was computer-randomized with balanced baseline characteristics and almost complete outcome data, the study was explicitly unblinded and its principal comparative advantages rest on patient-reported subjective outcomes (VAS pain, BCS comfort), giving high risk of bias in outcome measurement. Additional concerns about unreported allocation concealment, non-ITT handling of four excluded patients, and absence of a registered protocol/pre-specified outcomes support an overall high risk of bias.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly reports a prospective randomized controlled trial (NCT02067221) in which 70 consenting patients were allocated 1:1 to mini-PCNL or RIRS, with the randomization sequence generated by the institution's Department of Biostatistics and revealed to the surgeon only on admission the day before surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was generated centrally by a biostatistics department and concealed until the day before surgery (adequate concealment), but the sequence-generation method is not described, two patients were misallocated ("allocation error"), and there are two statistically significant baseline imbalances (hydronephrosis and S-ReSC stone-complexity score) in prognostically relevant stone/anatomic factors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization was carried out by the Department of Biostatistics of our institution and opened to the operating surgeon at the time of the patient's admission on the day before surgery." ... "the presence of hydronephrosis in the mini-PCNL group significantly less compared with the RIRS group (5/35, 14.3% versus 16/33, 48.5%; P=0.004). Seoul National University Renal Stone Complexity (S-ReSC) scores was 3.2 ± 1.9 in the mini-PCNL group and 2.1 ± 1.3 in the RIRS group (P=0.015)"

domain_judgments.rationale: Surgeon and patients were necessarily unblinded in this open surgical trial (relevant for the subjective pain/analgesic outcomes), and two randomized patients received the wrong intervention and were excluded rather than analysed by intention-to-treat, although the number affected is small (2/70).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Two patients from the RIRS group received mini-PCNL because of the allocation error and dropped out of the study." ... "Because of the allocation error, two patients in the RIRS group did not receive the allocated intervention and dropped out of the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 68/70 (97%) randomized participants, and the only two exclusions were due to an administrative allocation error unrelated to the outcome, so bias from missing data is unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of the 70 randomized patients, 68 completed the study including mini-PCNL in 35 and RIRS in 33."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (stone-free on non-enhanced CT) is objective and applied identically to both arms, but no blinding of outcome assessors/radiologists is reported, and the secondary subjective outcomes (VAS pain, as-needed analgesic use) were reported by unblinded patients managed by the single unblinded surgeon, which could influence those estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Stone-free status was defined as no residual stones or stones <2 mm on NECT within 3 months postoperatively." ... "All patients were asked about the pain severity by visual analogue score (VAS; range: 1-10) 1 hour postoperatively"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a clearly pre-specified primary endpoint and an a priori power calculation, but the registered protocol/analysis plan is not available for verification, many secondary outcomes were reported, and no adjusted analysis accounting for the significant baseline imbalances was presented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This prospective randomized controlled trial (NCT02067221) aimed to compare mini-PCNL and RIRS for renal stones >10 mm." ... "The primary endpoint in this study was SFR in a single session."

overall_summary: This registered 1:1 randomized trial had centrally generated, concealed allocation and near-complete follow-up (68/70), but raises some concerns from an unspecified sequence-generation method, two significant baseline imbalances (hydronephrosis, S-ReSC complexity score), a documented allocation error with exclusion of two patients rather than intention-to-treat analysis, and unavoidable lack of blinding affecting the subjective pain/analgesic outcomes. No domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is "some concerns".

design_rationale: The paper explicitly reports allocation by an online randomization tool: "the patients were randomized into either the RIRS group (Group 1) or PNL group (Group 2) in a ratio of 1:1 by using an online research randomizer", and is registered as a trial (NCT02430168).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although an online randomizer was used, allocation concealment is not described and there are large, highly significant baseline imbalances in key prognostic variables (stone number and stone burden, both P < .001) that directly plausibly affect pain and stone-free outcomes, which is not consistent with chance in a 1:1 randomized allocation of 100 patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The PNL group had significantly higher number of stones, greater stone burden... Stone size, mm 25.8 ± 5.3 / 30.84 ± 5.9, <.001"

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was impossible for surgical procedures (patients with nephrostomy tubes clearly knew their allocation, which can influence self-reported VAS pain), the analgesic protocol (escalation to tramadol) depended on unblinded clinical judgment, and no intention-to-treat analysis is described (132 enrolled but only 100 analyzed).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The operations were performed by a team of four experienced surgeons with at least 5 years of RIRS and PNL experience each."

domain_judgments.rationale: 132 patients were enrolled but only 100 (50 per group) are analyzed, and the text provides no account of the 32 missing participants or analysis of whether their exclusion biased the pain/analgesic results (the flow diagram is not legible in the available text).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of 132 patients ... were enrolled in this prospective study" ... "RIRS (n = 50) PNL (n = 50)"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome is participant-reported pain (VAS) and analgesic escalation decided by unblinded clinicians; patients necessarily knew which (visibly very different, tube-bearing versus stented) procedure they received, so outcome assessment could be influenced by knowledge of the intervention, and no blinded assessor or standardized escalation criteria are described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The patients who were included in the study were asked to fill out a visual analog scale (VAS) questionnaire at 8 and 24 hours postoperatively."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and a power calculation is mentioned, but the pre-specified primary outcome and analysis plan are not stated in the paper, multiple outcome operationalizations are reported (VAS at 8 and 24 hours, analgesic category, stone-free rate, complications), and the planned versus analyzed sample size differ, leaving some risk of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The national clinical trial number of our study is NCT02430168 ... Target population size was calculated with the G-Power software ... with a confidence interval of 0.80."

overall_summary: Despite nominal randomization and trial registration, the study shows large significant baseline imbalances in stone number and burden, unexplained attrition from 132 enrolled to 100 analyzed, and an unblinded, participant-reported primary outcome (VAS) with clinician-determined analgesic escalation. These issues in D1, D3, and D4 drive an overall high risk of bias.

design_rationale: The paper reports a prospective randomized clinical trial with 1:1 allocation generated by computer-generated random numbers ("All enrolled patients were randomized to mPNL group and RIRS group with allocation 1:1. The randomization was carried out using computer-generated random numbers"), registered at ChiCTR.

domain_judgments.rationale: Sequence generation was adequate (computer-generated) and baseline characteristics were well balanced, but allocation concealment is not described (sequence "opened to the operating surgeon before surgery" with no mention of sealed opaque envelopes or central allocation), leaving uncertainty about concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomization was carried out using computer-generated random numbers and opened to the operating surgeon before surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of patients and surgeons is impossible for these surgical procedures (inherent to the design), and the analysis excluded 5 randomized patients rather than following a strict intention-to-treat approach, though cross-over or protocol deviations are not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eventually, 5 patients withdrew during the treatment and follow-up phase, with 115 patients enrolled in the primary outcome analysis (58 in the mPNL group and 57 in the RIRS group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 5/120 (4.2%) participants were lost, balanced across arms (2 vs 3), so the small amount of missing data is unlikely to bias the stone-free rate estimate, although reasons for withdrawal are not specified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 5 patients withdrew during the treatment and follow-up phase, with 115 patients enrolled in the primary outcome analysis

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (stone-free status on CT with a pre-specified ≤3 mm threshold) is objective, measured identically in both groups, and assessors were reported to be blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The postoperative assessment was performed by investigators who were unaware of the patients’ group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a clearly pre-specified primary outcome (3-month SFR) and defined secondary outcomes, all of which appear to be reported, though the registry protocol was not directly compared in the text.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: this study was prospectively registered at http:// www.chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR1800016983)

overall_summary: This prospectively registered RCT had adequate random sequence generation, balanced baseline characteristics, minimal attrition, blinded outcome assessment of an objective CT-based endpoint, and no evident selective reporting. Overall risk is "some concerns" because allocation concealment is not described and the unavoidable lack of participant/surgeon blinding was combined with a non-intention-to-treat analysis excluding 5 randomized patients.
